sentences.t: The proposal covered 19 private land lots and part of a government road reserve in Section 9, Kota Damansara: two three-storey data centre blocks in a Selangor suburb.
On July 28, 2026 the project's consultant wrote to the Petaling Jaya City Council on the developer's behalf and withdrew the planning application.

The stated reason was that the developer wanted to re-examine the site and its components so the scheme would be "more economical, sustainable and compatible with development in the surrounding area."

The Gabungan Penduduk Kota Damansara coalition, speaking for more than 500 households, had objected over noise from round the clock operation, heat, high energy consumption, traffic and road safety, and the loss of government road reserve land. Residents said they would rather keep the plans for local shops.

Kota Damansara assemblyman Muhammad Izuan Ahmad Kasim confirmed the withdrawal: "The consultant has withdrawn the planning application for the data centre in Section 9, Kota Damansara." The Sungai Buloh MP Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Petaling Jaya councillor Muhamad Shazwan Suhaimi had both filed formal objections.
NEXTDC KL1 is about 11 kilometres away, two Google sites under construction in the Klang Valley about 16 kilometres away and Huawei Cloud Kuala Lumpur about 21 kilometres away.

unconfirmed: The developer behind the proposal is not named in the source reached, and no capacity in megawatts, floor area or investment figure was published. Whether a revised application has since been filed is not known.

sentences.t: This one was stopped by the governor, not the council. Oregon owned the land, and Tina Kotek ordered the state to pull out of the sale.

The California company Verrus had contracted in May 2025 to buy 32.23 acres at the Mill Creek Corporate Center in southeast Salem for a $5.1 billion data center, with the sale due to close in October 2026 and 75 permanent jobs promised.

Kotek announced the withdrawal on July 30, 2026: "This decision is about my responsibility to make sure state actions reflect Oregon's values and serve the public interest." She said she supports economic development, but "growth has to make sense for the community, for our infrastructure, and for our natural resources."

Salem resident Brian Hines said the protests were the most intense and emotional the city had seen on any subject. Another resident, Hannah Shooting Bear, put the objection in terms of the state's reputation: "when you start bringing these data centers in, that's not gonna be clean and green anymore."
Verrus said the decision was "made unilaterally and without consultation," before the company could present its design, infrastructure plan and community benefit proposals.
A second Verrus data center, marked suspended, sits about 9 kilometers away, two data centers in Marion County in all.

unconfirmed: Sources differ on the site area, our record giving 32 to 75 acres against the 32.23 acres reported here, and no capacity in megawatts or water figure was published. Whether Verrus will seek another Oregon site is not established.

sentences.t: Mary Eileen Flanagan told the supervisors what the water situation already is where she lives: "Many of my neighbors' wells have gone dry and require additional depth."

On August 26, 2026 the Pinal County Board of Supervisors voted 4 to 1 to reject the rezoning and development plans for the La Osa Energy Center, a data center campus proposed by Vermaland on about 3,300 acres outside Eloy.
The scheme covered 11 data center buildings, a 500 megawatt natural gas plant and battery storage, against a total demand of 1 gigawatt, which the reporting compared to powering a large city.

The revised proposal capped fresh water use at 600 acre-feet, roughly 200 million gallons, for the data centers and the gas plant together. On offsetting that, the developer committed only to considering the purchase of effluent water.

The power did not add up either. The developers said they had secured 500 megawatts of natural gas, half the 1 gigawatt demand. Supervisor Jeffrey McClure doubted the rest could be found in solar: "My understanding is that's dedicated to some other companies."

Robin Davis, from Hidden Valley, suggested the developers had asked for more than they wanted so they could settle for their real target. Mark Seidel, from Florence, told the board: "I don't want an incomplete and hastily built and ever-changing proposal."
Pinal County has no zoning definition or development requirement for data centers at all, which left water limits, noise rules and energy protections to whatever the developer chose to offer.

Another Vermaland project, proposed at 3,000 megawatts, sits about 25 kilometers away, and the proposed 600 megawatt Project Blue at Marana about 39 kilometers away. Marana has zoning limits in force.

unconfirmed: No investment figure for La Osa was published, and it is not known whether Vermaland intends to reapply or whether Pinal County has since written data center rules into its code.

sentences.t: The municipality asked for the environmental data for ten months. Mayor Renato Pasinetti said it never came.

East Gate withdrew its building application for a 120 megawatt data centre on a 130,000 square metre industrial area outside Travagliato, in the Brescia province of Lombardy. The withdrawal was reported on September 14, 2026.

The municipality had never received the environmental impact assessment data or the documentation needed to judge the grid connection. "To do that, we wanted the data. Which never arrived," Pasinetti said. He confirmed: "Yes, the proponents withdrew the building application for the implementation plan," and said the province would have no choice but to shelve the grid connection application.

The municipality had formally rejected the project the previous month. An online petition against it gathered nearly 10,000 signatures, with residents objecting to the energy consumption and the environmental consequences.
The proposal had promised more than 11 million euro of local economic benefit, including about 524,715 euro in compensation for agricultural land.
The friction is regional, with recent protests against a 240 megawatt facility at nearby Magenta.
Microsoft's Settala site, about 39 kilometres away, is the only other data centre recorded within range.

unconfirmed: Our record names the developer as East Gate or Edge Gate, noting the name differs by source, and the account reached uses East Gate. No investment figure was published beyond the local benefit offer, and no resident or petition organiser is quoted.

sentences.t: The county approved a lot merger and skipped the environmental review. A judge said it could not do that.

On September 9, 2026 Imperial County Superior Court Judge L. Brooks Anderholt overturned the county's approval of a data center of nearly 1 million square feet next to the Victoria Ranch residential neighbourhood, and ordered a full review under the California Environmental Quality Act.

The case was brought by the City of Imperial and the Sierra Club. The county had exempted the project from environmental review when it approved a lot merger in April 2026. Anderholt wrote that the county "prejudicially abused its discretion by approving the lot merger without first completing the CEQA review required for the whole project."
The complex includes a battery system, natural gas generators and a power substation, next to homes.

Mark West, a Sierra Club director, said: "I'm thrilled for the people of Imperial County. We want to understand the significant environmental impacts that this project is going to have." Imperial City Manager Dennis Morita called the ruling a step toward vindicating the city's position.
The developer, Sebastian Rucci, said: "We are disappointed but not deterred. We will seek a new trial and, if that motion is denied, appeal the ruling on the grounds outlined in our objections."
The local grid is small. The site sits in the Imperial Irrigation District control area, which peaks at about 1,123 megawatts.
A 330 megawatt Imperial data center is under construction about 23 kilometers away, with a 54 megawatt geothermal plant about 7 kilometers away and a 150 megawatt solar plant about 8 kilometers away.

unconfirmed: No capacity in megawatts, investment figure or timeline for the project was published, and no Victoria Ranch resident is quoted. The outcome of the new trial motion and any appeal was not established.
